transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
My daughter persuaded me to come here today, but I already know what is happening. I know people around my husband’s doctors are secretly working against us, and no one can convince me otherwise.
Can you tell me more about what makes you think people around your husband's doctors are working against you, and how long have you been feeling this way?

It all started about two years ago after my husband’s heart surgery, when I noticed certain neighbors and clinic staff whispering and sharing information about us. They started doing things like changing his appointment times and giving me strange looks, and I can tell it is a coordinated plan to block him from getting the right care. My daughter says it's just a coincidence, but I know they are working together against us.
Have you ever had any periods where you didn't believe that people were working against you, or has this feeling been constant over the past two years?

No, it has been completely constant ever since his surgery nearly two years ago. There hasn't been any time where those worries went away or where I felt like I could let my guard down. It has just been building up day after day.
Have you ever acted on these beliefs by, for example, confronting the people you think are against you, or have you kept them mostly to yourself and dealt with them in your own way?

I haven't openly confronted them, but I have taken my own steps to keep my husband safe. I insist on handling all of his medical appointments completely alone, double-check every interaction, and refused the home-health services they tried to send us. I've also had to step back from organizing my community events and seeing friends just to keep our lives secure.
Have you experienced any other unusual symptoms, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, or has it primarily been these concerns about people working against you and your husband?

No, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there; my mind is completely clear. This isn't some "unusual symptom" to me, but a very real situation where people are actively working against my husband's care and monitoring us. That is the only thing I am concerned about.

Can you describe how your beliefs about people working against you and your husband have evolved or changed over the two years since his surgery, and are there any specific events or evidence that you think prove your concerns are valid?

At first, it was just small things right after his surgery, like the clinic suddenly changing his appointment times and the nurses giving me cold, knowing looks. Over the two years, it became a clear pattern when I noticed certain neighbors whispering with the clinic staff and showing up at the same times. These aren't coincidences; they are the exact proof that there is a coordinated plan to interfere with his recovery.

Have you ever had any breaks or periods where your thoughts about people working against you seemed less real or less pressing, even if just for a short time, or have these thoughts remained consistently convincing to you?

No, they have never seemed less real or faded at all; they have been consistently convincing every single day for the last two years. Even though my daughter and others try to tell me it is just a coincidence, I simply cannot ignore clear signs like the moved appointments and those strange looks. I am absolutely certain of what is happening, and my mind has not changed.
Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning as a result of your beliefs about people working against you and your husband?

I still manage our home perfectly fine, including cooking, handling our bills, and keeping track of my husband's medications. However, because of these worries, I've turned down home-health services and stepped back from organizing community events, which has strained friendships with people who think I'm shutting them out. Aside from having to protect us and manage his appointments on my own, I am functioning completely normally.

You've mentioned that your beliefs about people working against you and your husband have been constant for two years, but can you describe if there have been any fluctuations in how strongly you believe in this conspiracy or how much it affects your daily life?

My belief has never fluctuated; it has been completely steady and building ever since my husband's surgery, and I remain absolutely certain of what is happening. While I did have to step back from community events and decline home-health services because of these concerns, my ability to manage our home, cook, handle our bills, and manage my husband's medications remains completely unaffected. I am doing all of those daily tasks just as well as I always have.

You've stated your belief in the conspiracy has been constant and unwavering, but can you think of any instance, no matter how small, where your confidence in this belief might have wavered or where you considered an alternative explanation, even if briefly?

No, my confidence has never wavered for even a second, and I have never considered any other explanation. The signs, like the rescheduled appointments and the strange looks from the nurse, are far too obvious and coordinated to be mere coincidences. No matter what my daughter or anyone else says, I remain absolutely certain of this interference.
